findings.evidence: Header and statements claim a destructive rollback of every standalone_001-created table, including DROP TABLE public.ewoh_production_task, public.ewoh_personnel, public.ewoh_organization and public.ewoh_ai_suggestion CASCADE.
findings.impact: Executing this rollback permanently deletes existing tenant, person, production-task and other pre-existing business tables and cascades dependent objects; this is catastrophic, cross-tenant production data loss.
findings.fix: Rewrite the rollback to distinguish newly created A-class tables from pre-existing B-class tables: drop only A-class tables, and for B-class tables remove additive columns, policies and RLS while preserving business rows, matching the documented SQL-038 contract.

findings.evidence: The database URL falls back to a connection string containing ewoh_owner:devownerpw, and the organization defaults to a fixed tenant UUID when --org-id is absent.
findings.impact: Credential material can leak into source/history and accidental invocation silently targets the default organization.

findings.evidence: The execution, feedback and KPI deletes run as three separate statements without BEGIN/COMMIT or ROLLBACK.
findings.impact: A failure after the first delete leaves partially cleared derived facts, which can make golden-path validation non-reproducible.
findings.fix: Wrap all deletes in one transaction, commit only after all succeed, and roll back cleanly on error.

contracts: Default dry-run; explicit --yes is required to write.
Scenario reset and purge operate within explicit transactions.
Purge uses a hardcoded table whitelist and UUID-validated organization id.
security_boundaries: Requires an explicit organization UUID and owner database URL.
Schema identifier is regex validated; table names come only from internal whitelists.
tenant_boundaries: Every destructive statement is organization-scoped; protected configuration tables are never purged.
failure_paths: Usage/schema/organization/database precondition errors abort without writes.
Database failure triggers ROLLBACK and propagates an error.
tests: Exported helpers support regression tests of parsing, dry-run and SQL construction.

findings.evidence: The ewoh_schedule_task time re-anchor is issued inside the reset transaction but .catch(() => undefined) suppresses its error.
findings.impact: A failed mirror-table update leaves schedule-task windows unshifted while production-task windows are committed, creating silent time-window inconsistency in the rerun scenario.
findings.fix: Remove the swallow-all catch, handle only the documented missing-table SQL state explicitly, and fail/rollback for any other update error.

contracts: Discovers standalone migrations and requires every file, command and rollback to be registered.

failure_paths: Registration mismatch, duplicate ID, missing dependency or cycle aborts planning.

tests: --plan exports the ordered migration contract for validation.
